newsitem.title: USA: CME hog futures close stronger, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hog futures close stronger, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures remained strong at the close on firm cash indications for Friday while pork bellies finished mixed as profit taking generally offset commercial buying interest, traders said.

Hog futures climbed through the day, led by October, on scattered buying linked to strength in cash markets. Cash hogs were expected to trade steady to mostly $0.50 per cwt higher Friday after as much as a $2.25 gain in cash hog prices Thursday, traders said.
Much of packer demand for cash hogs was coming from active pork sales.
"The product is moving well and packer competition seems to be strong," said Doug Harper, senior livestock analyst for Brock Associates Inc.
He added that exports are an underlying factor, including good domestic demand. "Domestically, we are moving the product at a pretty good clip here in the last week or two."
Most analysts are also looking for tight ham and belly stocks in Friday's monthly USDA Cold Storage report.
Rand Financials notably bought October and December late and also spread long October/short December, pit sources said.

In hog options, a local was actively doing the Delta neutral call spread, selling February 74 calls and buying 80 calls in a five to nine ratio early. Locals also bought October 56 calls, pit sources said.

Local profit taking ahead of the storage report and recent sharp advances offset continued commercial demand. Futures rallied seven cents in three days from recent lows and the market appeared overbought, traders said.
However, support was still evident from cash strength. Cash pork bellies sold up mostly $5 per cwt at $75 by the noon USDA report, the highest level since August 29, sources said.
"It looks to me like we still have a tight supply (of frozen) and overdid it to the downside (in futures) a week or two ago," Harper said.
But he noted that February is a long way off and profit taking will develop at times.
"We're talking clear out into February and it gets difficult to link the belly futures to fundamentals."
Hog futures closed 0.600 cent higher to unchanged with October up most at 56.125 cents a lb. Bellies finished 0.200 cent higher to 0.450 lower with February up most at 78.750 cents.
